## ctxloom mcp server set

Set fields of a bundle's MCP server from flags

### Synopsis

Set fields of a bundle-scoped MCP server without opening an editor.

Only the flags you pass change the entry; every other field keeps its stored
value. A name the bundle lacks is created. An empty value clears a field:
--url "" clears the url, and --arg "", --env "", --header "" or --tag ""
clears that list or map. A repeatable flag replaces the stored list or map
with exactly the values given; --env and --header take NAME=value.

A server has exactly one target: --command (with --arg), --url, or
--served-by session-endpoint. To move to another target, clear the old one in
the same call (the last example); a set that would leave none or two is
refused and nothing is saved.

Header values land in shell history and in committed bundle content, so name a secret through an environment variable the engine expands, never as a literal.

```
ctxloom mcp server set <bundle>#mcp/<name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  ctxloom mcp server set tools#mcp/search --url https://mcp.example.com/v1 --header X-Team=core --tag search
  ctxloom mcp server set tools#mcp/search --notes "Team search index"
  ctxloom mcp server set tools#mcp/search --url "" --header "" --command search-mcp --arg=--stdio
```

### Options

```
      --arg stringArray       Command argument (repeatable; replaces the list; "" clears it)
      --command string        Command that launches a stdio server ("" clears it)
      --env stringArray       Environment variable as NAME=value (repeatable; replaces the map; "" clears it)
      --header stringArray    HTTP header as Name=value (repeatable; replaces the map; "" clears it)
      --installation string   Setup instructions shown to the user ("" clears them)
      --notes string          Human-readable notes ("" clears them)
      --served-by string      "session-endpoint": the running session serves this entry ("" clears it)
      --tag stringArray       Tag (repeatable; replaces the list; "" clears it)
      --url string            Endpoint of a remote server, http or https ("" clears it)
```
